current.text: The projected starting lineup is James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.
Cleveland lost four rotation players: Max Strus, Dennis Schroder, Keon Ellis and Dean Wade.
The projected bench is Jaylon Tyson, Sam Merrill, Thomas Bryant, Nae'Qwan Tomlin and Craig Porter Jr.
Bench depth is clearly weaker than last season. Jaylon Tyson must play a lot.
Big-man depth is very thin. Behind Mobley and Allen there is only Thomas Bryant, then Ernest Udeh Jr. and Khalifa Diop.
Losing Dean Wade also removed the small-ball center option.

It is unclear whether Kenny Atkinson will play Mobley more at center in smaller lineups, possibly closing games that way with Watson, or lean into Allen and Harden pick-and-rolls. This choice drives Allen's minutes.
The second unit has no clear point guard, so Harden and Mitchell may stagger their minutes.
How much Harden and Mitchell play together is the key question for Mitchell's value.
Harden is now there for a full season, so more players need the ball. Harden's usage dropped in Cleveland, and his arrival cut into Mitchell's assists and scoring.
The backcourt is crowded with Harden and Mitchell, so rookies have no immediate role.
The season preview listed no current injury concerns for the team.
Cleveland is expected to be a very good team. Danny predicts about 51 to 53 wins, above the market win total, so tanking risk is low.
Coach Kenny Atkinson is under pressure.
Cleveland has among the most back-to-backs in the league, so rest risk for its older stars is higher than average.
With our March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and then 2 games in weeks 19 to 21. Week 21, the finals week starting March 22, is a two-game week. This is the weakest playoff schedule in the league.
From December 23 to February 6 the schedule has no consecutive home or road games.
That heavy travel stretch could hurt the team's play.

tags.detail: 4, 3 and 2 games in weeks 19 to 21. 9 games in total, rank 30 of 30, with a two-game finals week.

tags.name: many back-to-backs

tags.name: thin bench
tags.detail: Lost Strus, Schroder, Ellis and Wade. Only Thomas Bryant behind Mobley and Allen.
tags.new_meaning: The team has little bench depth, so starters carry heavy loads and an injury opens a big role for a reserve.

tags.name: contender
tags.detail: Win total 47.5 (rank 9). Danny predicts 51 to 53 wins.
tags.new_meaning: The team is expected to be among the better teams, so tanking is unlikely.

note: Cleveland is a strong team, so tanking is unlikely. The cost is in the schedule: it has among the most back-to-backs and the worst playoff weeks in the league, with only 2 games in our finals week. That lowers the value of every Cav, mostly Harden and Mitchell, who also share the ball and cut into each other's usage. The thin bench and thin frontcourt boost Jaylon Tyson and make Thomas Bryant a real handcuff. Early on, watch how often Harden and Mitchell stagger and whether Atkinson closes games with Mobley at center, since that would cost Allen minutes.
